chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: From here on out, I'm going to assume that you want to be a hedge fund manager.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And one of your first tasks as a hedge fund manager is to get investors.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So who might your investors be?

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: There are three major types of investors in hedge funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Of course, there's others besides these, but these are the three main types.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Individuals, in other words, a single person that wants to invest in a fund.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Of course, these are typically very wealthy folks.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Keep in mind that hedge funds typically can only have up to 100 investors.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So they want each of those investments to be fairly large so

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: that they can manage, of course, a significant amount of funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So the individuals who invest in hedge funds are typically, as I said, very wealthy.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Institutions, what do I mean by institution?

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: These are things like very large retirement funds, like CalPERS out in California.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: These are university foundations, like the Harvard University Foundation or the Georgia Tech Foundation.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: In other words, institutions, very often nonprofit institutions, that have a large sum of money that they need to keep somewhere.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And, of course, they'd like to see an accrual in value.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So that's one reason they look to hedge funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And finally, funds of funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: What funds of funds do is they group together the funds of many individuals or institutions.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So, for instance, you might be an individual that could, say, invest in one hedge fund, but you'd really like to get the advantage of investing in several funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So you might allow your money to be collected by a manager of funds of funds.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And then that manager would gather together all these assets and pick carefully several hedge funds to invest that money in.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So besides knowing who your investors might be, it's critically important to know why they might invest in your fund.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: How can you present the case to them that will convince them that they should let you manage their money?

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Here are at least some of the criteria that folks like this would consider before investing in a hedge fund.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Track record.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: So if your fund has a great track record, that's, of course, some of the best evidence that it's going to continue to work well.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Many institutional investors will want to see a good track record for at least five years before they'll invest in a particular fund.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Now, if you're a young whippersnapper hedge fund manager and you don't have five years yet, what are you going to do?

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: Well, what you can do is simulate or backtest your strategy.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And investors will consider these simulations, but that simulation has to be backed by a very compelling story describing that strategy.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: In other words, you've got to have a reason for why this method works and it needs to make sense.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: And finally, they consider how your strategy fits within their portfolio.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: In other words, if your strategy is for large cap S&P 500 stocks and they've already got that covered with another fund, they might not consider you.

chunks.title: How funds attract investors
chunks.text: However, if you, for instance, are looking at small cap growth stocks and they don't yet have that part of their portfolio filled, they'll give you some more thought.
